newsitem.title: LEBANON: U.S. group cites Syrian abuses in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. group cites Syrian abuses in Lebanon.

text.p: A U.S.-based human rights group has urged Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri to work to end what it said was the abduction of Lebanese citizens and Palestinian refugees by Syrian security forces in Lebanon.

"Human Rights Watch/Middle East is writing to express our deep concern about the abduction and interrogation of Lebanese citizens and Palestinian refugees by Syrian security forces in Lebanon," the group said in letter to Hariri.
It said its representatives learned during a recent visit to Lebanon of two disappearances in July.
Hariri will meet U.S. President Bill Clinton at the White House on Friday. A copy of the letter dated October 11 was faxed to an international news agency in Beirut on Thursday.
Human Rights Watch, a Washington-based privately funded group, said the abductions were followed by transfer to Syria for imprisonment without charge or any form of due process.
The group urged Hariri to take measures to end the abuses, including a public declaration "that Syrian forces will no longer be permitted to operate with impunity on Lebanese soil".
Syria has some 35,000 troops stationed over two-thirds of Lebanon, making it Beirut's main power broker.

The group said Hariri should also issue written instructions to the Lebanese judiciary and police to institute procedures for taking written complaints about "disappearances" and establish a special office with full authority to investigate such cases.

"We believe the affirmative steps suggested above will help break the barrier of fear that paralyses families from coming forward when 'disappearances' occur and discourages lawyers from providing legal representation," the group added.
It said it had received complaints that Lebanese security forces took part in handing over their own citizens to the Syrians, "who use torture to elicit information during interrogation".

It quoted a Lebanese man as saying earlier this year that he was tortured by Syrian security forces in Beirut after being taken from his home after midnight at gunpoint, blindfolded, handcuffed and in his pyjamas.
